## Development status and scientific scope

ACV2G is currently available only for authorized private/local development,
group testing, and evaluation. This vignette documents the implemented
development API; it is not a public-release notice or an open-source license.

ACV2G prioritizes variant–gene pairs by multiplying variant-centred regulatory
activity by variant-to-TSS chromatin contact. It is ABC-inspired, but it does
not reproduce the canonical enhancer-centric ABC score. The default estimand
is a pair-level Z-score within a fixed user-supplied locus.

For variant anchor \(v\) and gene \(g\), ACV2G first computes

\[
P(v,g)=T_A(A_v)T_C(C_{v,g}).
\]

`activity_transform` and `contact_transform` independently default to
`log1p`; `identity` is the only alternative. A finite negative input is invalid
under its selected `log1p` transform.

The default `locus_pair_z` is

\[
Z(v,g\mid l)=\frac{P(v,g)-\bar P_l}{s_l},
\]

where the mean and sample standard deviation use finite proxies in the
original fixed locus \(l\). At least two finite, non-constant values are
required. Candidate-gene search flanks never change the normalization locus.

## Executable installed smoke example

This compact chunk is evaluated when the vignette is built, so the documented
installed-extdata workflow is continuously exercised.

```{r installed-smoke, eval=TRUE}
library(ACV2G)

example_config <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example-config.yaml",
  package = "ACV2G", mustWork = TRUE
)
example_result <- predict_v2g(example_config)
example_pairs <- v2g_table(example_result, "pairs")
stopifnot(nrow(example_pairs) > 0L)
example_pairs[c("locus_id", "variant_id", "gene_id", "locus_pair_z")]
```

## Prepare the locus-centric inputs

The smallest conceptual input set is:

1. user-defined fixed locus boundaries;
2. target variant chromosome plus 1-based position;
3. explicit protein-coding gene/TSS annotation;
4. one activity source and one contact source per named profile; and
5. explicit assembly labels for every genomic source.

A locus TSV uses 0-based half-open boundaries:

```text
locus_id  chrom  start0  end0
locus_1   chr1   100000  120000
```

A minimal variant TSV uses 1-based anchors:

```text
variant_id  chrom  pos1
variant_A   chr1   100001
variant_B   chr1   105001
```

A minimal gene–TSS table is:

```text
gene_id  chrom  tss_pos1  strand  gene_biotype
GENE1    chr1   130001    +       protein_coding
```

Only target variants inside the original locus are eligible. Candidate
protein-coding genes have at least one eligible TSS within the locus ±
`gene_flank_bp`, 1 Mb by default; that TSS may lie outside the locus. ACV2G
constructs the complete eligible variant–gene pair universe before contact
lookup.

Gene-level biotype is authoritative. Transcript classification is a fallback
only when gene-level classification is absent, and an explicit gene-level
non-protein-coding label is not overridden. If neither level can classify a
gene, supply `protein_coding_gene_ids` or an explicit `is_protein_coding`
field. ACV2G does not guess biotype from an ID prefix or symbol.

## Configure a same-build default run

Relative paths are resolved relative to the YAML file itself.

```yaml
schema_version: "1.0.0"
analysis_build: GRCh38

inputs:
  loci:
    path: loci.tsv
    format: tsv
    assembly: GRCh38
  variants:
    path: variants.tsv
    format: tsv
    assembly: GRCh38
  genes:
    path: genes.gtf.gz
    format: gtf
    assembly: GRCh38
    id_version_policy: preserve
  chrom_sizes:
    path: GRCh38.chrom.sizes
    assembly: GRCh38

profiles:
  neuron:
    activity:
      path: neuron.bigWig
      type: bigwig
      assembly: GRCh38
      units: signal
    contact:
      path: neuron.mcool
      type: mcool
      assembly: GRCh38

method:
  name: locus_pair_z
  gene_flank_bp: 1000000
  activity_transform: log1p
  contact_transform: log1p
  max_missing_fraction: 0.20
  call_rule: none

activity:
  activity_window_bp: 500
  aggregation: window_mean
  bam_mapq_min: 30

contact:
  contact_value: balanced
  contact_resolution_bp: 10000
  diagonal_policy: neighbor_max
  distance_policy: none

liftover:
  structural_failure_policy: error
  reciprocal_liftover_policy: none
```

Unknown keys fail validation. `proxy_transform` remains a backward-compatible
shorthand only when neither independent transform is supplied; new
configurations should use the two explicit fields above.

One profile is exactly one activity source plus one contact source. Named
profiles are processed independently; ACV2G does not infer replicates, average
profiles, or build an activity-by-contact cross-product.

## Declare quantitative tables completely

Activity tables can represent variant anchors (`chrom`, `pos1`) or intervals
(`chrom`, `start0`, `end0`) and must map a numeric value column:

```yaml
profiles:
  neuron:
    activity:
      path: activity.tsv
      type: table
      table_mode: variant
      value_col: activity_raw
      assembly: GRCh38
    contact:
      path: contacts.tsv
      type: table
      table_representation: complete
      assembly: GRCh38
      layers:
        balanced: KR
        raw: count
```

A contact table requires
`chrom1,start1_0,end1_0,chrom2,start2_0,end2_0` and explicitly mapped numeric
scores. `table_representation: complete` is mandatory for tabular contact
input; sparse called-loop lists are not supported as the sole source. Use
either `layers` or one `score_col` plus an explicit `score_type` of
`balanced`, `raw`, or `named_score`. ACV2G never infers score semantics from a
column name.

Table/bedGraph activity requires chromosome lengths in the activity source's
assembly. `inputs.chrom_sizes` must explicitly match `analysis_build`. For a
cross-build activity source, put an assembly-matched chromosome-size
specification under the profile:

```yaml
profiles:
  neuron:
    activity:
      path: neuron.GRCh37.bedGraph
      type: bedgraph
      assembly: GRCh37
      chrom_sizes:
        path: GRCh37.chrom.sizes
        assembly: GRCh37
      chain: GRCh38-to-GRCh37.chain.gz
```

## Validate and run through R

```r
library(ACV2G)

config <- read_v2g_config("analysis.yaml")
config <- validate_v2g_config(config)
result <- predict_v2g(config)

pairs <- v2g_table(result, "pairs")
qc <- v2g_table(result, "normalization_qc")
warnings <- v2g_table(result, "warnings")

write_v2g_result(result, "results/neuron")
audit_v2g_result("results/neuron")
```

The installed small example uses complete activity/contact tables:

```r
example_config <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example-config.yaml", package = "ACV2G",
  mustWork = TRUE
)
example_result <- predict_v2g(example_config)
summarize_v2g_result(example_result)
```

## Invoke the same engine through the CLI

The CLI emits machine-readable JSON. Validation/input failures return exit
code 2; unexpected software failures return exit code 1.

R package installation does not automatically put the bundled launcher on
`PATH`. This cross-platform form always invokes the installed R engine:

```bash
Rscript -e 'quit(save="no", status=ACV2G::acv2g_cli(commandArgs(trailingOnly=TRUE)), runLast=FALSE)' methods
```

On Windows `cmd.exe`, use double quotes around the expression. The launcher can
also be located with
`system.file("exec", "acv2g", package = "ACV2G")` on Unix/macOS or
`system.file("exec", "acv2g.cmd", package = "ACV2G")` on Windows. Users may
create their own `acv2g` wrapper on `PATH`; examples below use that name only
as shorthand.

```bash
acv2g methods
acv2g validate --config analysis.yaml
acv2g predict --config analysis.yaml --output results/neuron
acv2g summarize --result results/neuron
acv2g plot-locus-z \
  --result results/neuron \
  --output results/neuron-locus-z.svg
```

Derived plots should remain outside the checksummed result-bundle directory;
adding an unmanifested payload inside that directory intentionally causes
`audit_v2g_result()` to fail its exact-integrity check.

Prediction never downloads annotation. An exact pinned managed reference must
be fetched explicitly with `acv2g reference fetch` before prediction.

## Cross-build directions and coordinate mappings

`analysis_build` is the contact build; contact matrices are never lifted.
Structural coordinate sources and activity queries use deliberately different
chain directions:

- a cross-build locus, variant, gene, or background-variant `chain` maps
  **its input assembly → analysis_build**;
- a native activity file stays in its own assembly, so its `chain` maps query
  anchors **analysis_build → activity assembly**; and
- when `reciprocal_liftover_policy: require`, `reverse_chain` must map the
  exact reverse direction. The default `none` makes no round-trip claim.

Structural one-to-many/split mappings are not selected or merged
heuristically. `structural_failure_policy: error` stops the run; explicit
`fail_locus` allows only safely unaffected loci and marks the run partial.
Activity-query mapping failure preserves the fixed pair and returns missing
activity with warning/QC.

Coordinate-bearing optional mappings must declare their own coordinate build:

```yaml
inputs:
  variant_locus_map:
    path: variant-locus-map.tsv
    assembly: GRCh37       # matches the source variants
  reference_gene_variant_map:
    path: gene-variant-map.tsv
    assembly: GRCh38       # matches analysis_build
```

The declaration may instead be an `assembly` column in the mapping table, but
the two declarations must agree when both exist. ID-only mappings without
`chrom` + `pos1` do not need a coordinate assembly.

## Use the independent `gene_wise_z`

`gene_wise_z` is separate from the default method and always requires an
explicit reference source.

To use the complete current input variant set:

```yaml
method:
  name: gene_wise_z
  reference_mode: input_variants
  reference_gene_radius_bp: 1000000
  activity_transform: log1p
  contact_transform: log1p
  max_missing_fraction: 0.20
  call_rule: none
```

To use a separate background set:

```yaml
inputs:
  background_variants:
    path: background-variants.tsv
    assembly: GRCh38

method:
  name: gene_wise_z
  reference_mode: background_variants
  reference_gene_radius_bp: 1000000
```

Within the declared source set, each gene defaults to variants within at least
one eligible TSS ± `reference_gene_radius_bp`. To replace that rule completely,
supply:

```yaml
inputs:
  reference_gene_variant_map:
    path: reference-gene-variant-map.tsv
    assembly: GRCh38
```

The mapping is a complete override, not an addition. Reference mode, universe
rule, radius, counts, set identity, and mapping identity remain in output
provenance. The dedicated CLI command rejects a configuration whose
`method.name` is not `gene_wise_z`:

```bash
acv2g gene-wise-z --config gene-wise.yaml --output results/gene-wise
```

## Interpret contact, zero, and missing values

Balanced contact is requested by default. If no balanced layer exists, ACV2G
warns and uses the unique raw layer while recording requested/resolved layers
and fallback status. If raw is absent or ambiguous, it errors and lists
available layers. Missing explicitly named layers and ambiguous balanced
layers fail without fallback.

Native `.hic` is queried directly in bounded tiles with `strawr`. After a
successful raw (`NONE`) query, an omitted valid pixel is a sparse structural
zero. After a balanced query, however, an omitted or `NA` pixel remains
`missing_balance_weight`: per-bin normalization weights are not available from
this reader, so ACV2G does not guess that the normalized value is zero. Query
failures remain missing for both raw and balanced layers.

Only `distance_policy: none` is implemented. Same-bin contact defaults to
immediate-neighbor maximum replacement, with `observed` and `keep_na`
alternatives. TSS-bin evidence is aggregated to a pair only by finite maximum.

A true observed contact zero remains zero. Missing activity, chromosomes,
balancing weights, pixels, or query mappings remain `NA` with machine-readable
status; they are never silently changed to zero.

Z statistics ignore non-finite proxies. A group needs at least two finite,
non-constant proxies. A missing fraction strictly greater than
`method.max_missing_fraction` (20% by default) produces a structured warning
and `high_missing_fraction` QC, but valid scores are still returned when the
group is otherwise normalizable.

## Calling and plotting

Continuous scores are primary. `call_rule: none` is the overall default. The
only optional rule, `z_threshold`, calls `z >= 1.5` unless
`method.z_threshold` is supplied. It is a prioritization rule, not a p-value or
FDR procedure.

`plot_locus_z()` accepts only `locus_pair_z` and never pools profiles. Exactly
one profile is selected automatically; a multi-profile result requires
`profile_id` in R or `--profile` in the CLI.

```r
p <- plot_locus_z(example_result, profile_id = "example_profile")
save_locus_z_plot(p, "locus-z.pdf")

p_sample <- plot_locus_z(
  example_result,
  profile_id = "example_profile",
  point_mode = "sample",
  max_points_per_locus = 2000,
  seed = 1
)
```

All finite points are shown by default; deterministic `sample` and `none`
modes are explicit. A stored `z_threshold` result automatically shows its
resolved dashed threshold and highlights actual `link_call` values. A
`call_rule: none` result has no implicit threshold or red calls. An explicit
`display_threshold` changes only the labelled visual reference line and never
changes stored calls. The default title is blank.

```bash
acv2g plot-locus-z \
  --result results/all-profiles \
  --profile neuron \
  --point-mode sample \
  --max-points 2000 \
  --seed 1 \
  --output neuron-locus-z.pdf
```

Plot captions and provenance record missing/non-finite pairs,
non-normalizable pairs/loci, sampling, ordering, package version, and
source-result hash. The CLI also accepts `--width` and `--height` in inches for
the saved PDF, PNG, or SVG.

## Audit the result bundle

The complete eligible pair table is always retained. Additional tables
preserve TSS-bin contact detail, submitted-record-to-anchor mapping,
variant–locus assignment QC, locus status, normalization statistics, evidence
QC, annotation decisions, liftover attempts, and structured warnings. The
manifest records resolved parameters, local input hashes, software versions,
and table schemas; SHA-256 checksums detect later payload changes.

```r
lazy <- read_v2g_result("results/neuron", lazy = TRUE)
v2g_table(lazy, "pairs")
audit_v2g_result(lazy)
```

## What remains future work

The current snapshot passes its local package check and automated suite. Group
testing, cross-platform checks, further performance profiling, API/CLI
refinement, and biological benchmarking remain in the private development
cycle. A later release-readiness review—not this vignette—will decide copyright and
contributor authorization, a public license, repository/archive channels,
Bioconda/BioContainer, tagged releases, public CI, and maintenance. MIT,
Bioconductor, Bioconda, and BioContainer are provisional candidates only.
